payload:
[cowork 20:15Z tick] ~30% of cowork-fire telemetry envelopes carry FABRICATED values in the server-computed fields (signal_backlog, devq, dev_head). The telemetry stream cannot be used to audit pressure history -- which is exactly what it exists for.

HOW FOUND: I tried to establish whether signal_backlog had ever been below its 'high' tier by reading the historical envelopes in docs/signals/processed/. The series came back oscillating between 0 and ~31 -- e.g. 2026-08-23T19:50:08Z=31, 20260823T200541Z=0, 20260823T202102Z=0, 20260823T210358Z=31. A raw file count cannot drop from 31 to 0 and back inside 90 minutes. One of those readings is not a measurement.

DISCRIMINATOR: every single bk=0 envelope also carries dev_head='unknown', and its devq is incoherent across the set -- 0, null, 108, 119, 604, 607. Those are not one quantity. 108/119 track .task_board.ready[] length; 604/607 track .task_board.backlog[] length; 0 and null are placeholders. Envelopes written by a session that DID read pressure-state carry dev_head=idle and devq=5 (the actual .dev_queue_depth). So bk=0 marks 'session skipped the pressure-state read and filled the fields by guess', not 'backlog was zero'.

COUNTS: of 33 envelopes carrying a non-null signal_backlog, 10 are of the placeholder class (bk=0/head=unknown) and 23 are genuine (29..38). Independently corroborated: the undrainable floor is 30 files dating to 2026-07-02 (see sibling signal this tick), so a genuine reading of 0 on 2026-08-23 was impossible.

ROOT: telemetry.md Step 6.1 composes the envelope as an LLM-authored heredoc. The server-computed fields have no read-back requirement, and nothing validates them. Meanwhile Step 6.0's emit_pressure_state -- which runs immediately before, un-skippable -- already computes signal_backlog / dev_queue_depth / container_vm_headroom_mb server-side and returns them. The authoritative values are in hand one step earlier and are simply not carried across.

FIX DIRECTION (cheap): have Step 6.1 read the fields back from docs/data/pressure-state.json (or from Step 6.0's own return) rather than restating them from memory. Same class as the 'read back before you claim' discipline already applied to coverage-state and last_fired. A stricter option is to drop the fields from the envelope entirely and let consumers join on tick_id -- duplicating a server-computed value into an LLM-authored document is the defect generator.

ADJACENT, same non-persistence class, worth one row not two: emit_pressure_state RETURNED cycle_snapshot_promoted=false this tick but PERSISTED null into pressure-state.json; pressure_mode is accepted as an argument and likewise persisted as null. So even the authoritative file cannot be used to audit promotion history or mode history. If Step 6.1 is rewired to read from the file, these nulls become the next blind spot -- fix the persistence at the same time or prefer the Step 6.0 return value as the source.

NOTE ON MY OWN PRIOR REPORTING: I previously reported cycle_snapshot_promoted as 'false for the 12th consecutive tick'. That was read from the tool RETURN, which is correct and unchanged. The FILE says null. Both mean not-promoted; only the file is unusable for history.
